# Stripping the frame

Pulled every component off the old steel frame down to bare metal before deciding whether the
restoration was even worth doing. Frame serial number is stamped under the bottom bracket shell:
WSBC-4417-982, which turned out to date it to a run from the early 1990s once I cross-referenced it.

## What came off

Full groupset, both wheels, headset, bottom bracket, seatpost, and the (surprisingly stuck)
stem. The bottom bracket cup on the drive side had to come out with a breaker bar and a lot of
penetrating oil — twenty-plus years of the same grease had basically welded it in place.

## Surface condition

Mostly surface rust, no pitting deep enough to worry about structural integrity. A few chips down to
bare metal near the drivetrain side, probably from a chain that dropped one too many times over the
years. Nothing that changes the plan to keep this frame rather than replace it.

## Paint decision

Going with a powder coat rather than a rattle-can respray — costs more but should hold up far better
than anything from a can, and a local shop quoted a reasonable price for a small frame like this one.
Color is still undecided; leaning toward the original factory shade rather than anything flashy.
